nodes.name: thm:network
nodes.statement:
Consider a sequence of graphs $\mathcal{G}_1,\mathcal{G}_2,\cdots,\mathcal{G}_m,\cdots$ such that Problem~(11) admits a feasible solution with $\Omega(m^k)$ unopened facilities and unserved customers, with $0<k<g(r)$. Let $m^*(\varepsilon,T)$ and $m^{\textsc{L}}(T)$ be the solution of Problem~(10) and the fully-learned solution. As $m \to \infty$, Algorithm~ALG_network yields a feasible solution to Problem~(10) and achieves a cost of
    $$m^\dagger(\varepsilon, T)\leq m^*(\varepsilon, T)+\begin{cases}
    	o\left(m^{\alpha_T \cdot (1-r)}\right)& \text{if }p=1 \text{ or } (p \neq 1 \text{ and } \alpha_T\cdot(1-r)>1/2)\\
    	\mathcal{O}(m^{1/2}) & \text{if }p \neq 1\text{ and } \alpha_T\cdot(1-r)\leq 1/2
    \end{cases}$$
    Moreover, assume that $\delta = o\left(m^{\alpha_T\cdot(1-r)-1}\right)$ and that $p=1$ or if the facilities of degree $d_\star$ can cover $\Omega(m)$ customers. Then the following holds: $m^*(\varepsilon, T)= m^{\textsc{L}}(T)+\Theta\left(m^{g(r)}\right)$.
